original_card.question: Can one specified masked or overcomplete decoder improve the complete moment budget?
methods: Synthesize a decoder with exact coefficients and fully priced helper endpoints.
Bound the best possible budget for a fixed support alphabet before synthesis.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound and count all copied information, frames and restoration.

first_step.inspect: Locate the excluded classes: masked identities, at least nine terms, and deeper punctures.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose one finite support alphabet and test exact decoding constraints before building a whole network.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A cheaper fully realized decoder could increase deficit or lower recursive cost on the binding complex side.
allowed_variations: Select a specific masked or overcomplete family with exact labels and supports.
scope_change_triggers: Repeating the exact eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

actual_scope: For the pinned P112 coordinate readers and exactly two added totals, do source unions of size 49, 50 or 51 lower the separate-total pairing-rank sum below the union-48 full-rank floor?
scope_change_reason: The card allows one specified overcomplete family. The eight-term all-pairs theorem excludes ten-term decoders, and the fixed-reader two-total screen was previously closed only through source union 48. This note keeps those eight coordinate readers and prices unions 49, 50 and 51. It does not repeat the eight-term all-pairs search. Frame and restoration charges are set to zero, which is the direction that could only help a negative copy-rank screen.
bottleneck_link: The complex primitive binds the selected conditional kappa. A two-total decoder whose fully charged moment beat the current complex budget would have to lower this copy-rank sum or move the child histogram. Unions 49-51 do not lower the full-rank on-column copy-rank sum below 65, so they do not by themselves improve kappa.
stop_rule: Stop after the closed-support census through size 51, the size-36 budget comparison, the cut search, and the single-codeword search at cap 51 are complete, whether or not the loss bound rises.
evidence: verify.py prints PASS_P112_TWO_TOTAL_UNION49_51. Retained loss stays 5 at caps 49, 50 and 51; the full-rank on-column floor stays 65; the union-48 witness bill is 74. No closed support has size 49 or 51.
author: AI-assisted research session
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance was used for the mathematics, implementation, verification and writing. No independent human review is claimed.

open_questions.question: Does source union 52 raise the fixed-reader two-column retained loss above 5?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Cap 52 is the first point at which a size-40 lead has a 12-port outside budget, so the cut-only reduction no longer applies to those leads. A loss of 7 or more would drop the full-rank relaxation to 64 or below.
open_questions.first_step: Enumerate closed supports of size 52 and test condition N on every lead whose outside budget is still below 12.
open_questions.blocked_by: Size-40 leads at cap 52 need the widened companion enumeration. This package only shows that widening a size-36 lead from 12 ports to 15 adds nothing.

open_questions.question: Is the full-rank on-column floor 65 attained by any loss-5 two-total correction?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The proved floor is a price relaxation. The explicit witness costs 74. If every loss-5 shape costs at least 66, the stronger floor extends through union 51.
open_questions.first_step: For each N-satisfying loss-5 shape, compute the minimum support of a nonzero vector in the correction column space and apply the 12/12 cut sign balance.
open_questions.blocked_by: Shapes other than one four-dimensional lead plus a single cut have free coordinate entries. This package does not solve those systems.
